judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's verified list is right, item for item: 8 cups of raisins for 12 cups of oats via 4, 6, 8 (p1); 12.50/5 = 2.50 (p2); 28, 42, 70 pages (p3); x = 12 cm (p4); 2.50 < 2.90 (p5); 174/6 = 29 mpg (p6); 10 cups of water (p7); 35 ounces (p8); 9/40 = 0.225 > 7/32 = 0.21875 so runner A (p9); 1050/3 = 350 and 1750/350 = 5 gallons (p10); 6/9 = 10/15 so equal win rates (p11); 2/5 > 3/8 with 14 and 9 cups (p12). Representation choice really is required rather than announced. But the judge scored answer_key_quality 4 without opening the Quick Answers bank, which prints '5. --', '9. --', '11. --' and '12. --, 14, 9'. This sheet declares no manual items whatsoever, so all four dashes are relations that verify.json holds and that passed; problems 5, 9 and 11 have no other answer, so a quarter of the bank is blank. The judge also did not weigh the open prompts: 7(a) 'Explain what is wrong with adding to both parts', 2 'Say why a unit rate is the useful representation here' and 3 'Which column did you find easiest, and why?' are all written answers with no manual entry, and final_response.md states the omission was deliberate.

strengths_to_preserve: Method choice is genuinely forced rather than announced: tables where the multiplier is friendly (1, 3), proportions where it is not (4, 8), unit rates where a per-one value is needed downstream (2, 6, 10), and direct comparisons that only work after both sides are in the same form (5, 9, 11). The key's Step 1 always says WHY that tool fits before any arithmetic, which is what makes the interleaving teachable.

Problem 9's key adds the observation that changes the answer's direction: 'minutes per kilometre works too, but then the smaller number wins (4.44 against 4.57). Say which form you used before deciding which direction is better.' That is the actual hazard in rate comparison and it is rarely written down.

Problem 12 makes the synthesis do real work -- compare concentration (2/5 > 3/8) BEFORE scaling either recipe, then scale each separately (14 and 9 cups) -- and the key closes by naming why three different tools appear inside one problem.

root_causes.description: Every compare entry's relation is dropped by render_quick_answers._fmt(), which returns the manual glyph '---' when sympify raises on '<', '>' or '='. Because this sheet has no manual items, four bank rows lose their only content.
evidence: verify.json ids 5, 9, 11 and 12 each hold a compare entry with order 'relation' (expected '<', '>', '=' and '>'), all passing (18 checks, gate_log verify-ws PASS)
Problem 11's printed task is exactly 'state the comparison using <, > or =', so its bank row is now empty of information
scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 56-61 return '---' on SympifyError; lines 71-73 use the same glyph for manual-only ids

root_causes.description: Written prompts were deliberately left unflagged because each sits beside a machine-checked number, which is precisely the case the prompt's instruction covers ('clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review').
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7(a): 'Explain what is wrong with adding to both parts'; verify.json id 7 holds one eval entry (10) and no manual entry
Problem 2 'Say why a unit rate is the useful representation here' and problem 3 'Which column did you find easiest, and why?' have no entries beyond their numeric parts
Problems 5, 9 and 11 each end by naming a winner (corner store, runner A, neither team) with no check behind the name
final_response.md: 'Nothing on this sheet is flagged for manual review -- the written say which representation you chose parts sit alongside answers that are all machine-checked'

improvements.title: Print the four verified relations instead of blanking a quarter of the bank
improvements.proposed_change: Teach the Quick Answers bank to render a verified relation. In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, render_entry() should special-case an entry whose type is 'compare' with order 'relation': build the line from the entry's own `values` and `expected`, e.g. `$34 < 34.2$`, instead of handing the bare string '<' to _fmt(). _fmt() must stop returning '---' for a relation token, and '---' must remain reserved for items that carry no `expected` at all (genuine manual review), so the two states are visually distinct on the page.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py gains this case's id 11: a single compare entry ['6/9','10/15'] expected '='. Assert the rendered line reads '$6/9 = 10/15$' and contains no '---'. render_entry returns '---' today, so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 5, 9 and 11 regain a bank answer they currently do not have, and problem 12's first part stops being a dash. On a sheet with zero manual items, no '---' should appear at all after the fix -- that is the clean post-condition to assert.
improvements.risk: Low; one formatting function. Compile the fixture key inside the test so an escaping slip cannot reach a delivered PDF.

improvements.title: Flag 7(a), 2 and 3's written prompts rather than declaring the sheet fully machine-checked
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual-coverage gate to the build chain. A new checker (tests/check_manual_coverage.py, wired into scripts/build.sh beside answer-line-ws) segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.py and, for each problem, scans the printed prose for open-response cues -- 'Explain', 'Why did/does', 'Say why', 'What went wrong', 'describe', 'in one or two sentences', 'Which ... did/was' followed by a rule blank, and the drawing verbs 'Plot', 'Shade', 'Draw', 'label' -- and requires the matching id in verify.json to carry at least one entry of type 'manual'. Exit 1 with the offending sentence quoted when it does not. SKILL.md line 257 already states the rule ('Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer'); nothing enforces it, and per-problem coverage (SKILL.md line 189) is satisfied by any single machine entry on the same id.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_manual_coverage.py gains a fixture from problem 7: a segment printing '(a) Explain what is wrong with adding to both parts' and '(b) Give the correct number of cups of water', with a verify.json id 7 holding only the eval for 10. Assert the checker exits 1 quoting the 'Explain' clause; add a manual entry and assert exit 0. The whole chain is green on this input today, so the test fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The delivered claim in final_response.md ('nothing is flagged for manual review') becomes accurate instead of a decision to treat explanations as covered by their numeric neighbours. Suite-wide this is the second-largest cluster (36 cases).
improvements.risk: A machine_first task could end up reporting several manual items, which reads as a regression to a user who wanted auto-grading. Report them as exit 2 (green with manual review) and keep the cue list narrow so reflective asides do not trigger it.

case_summary: Twelve interleaved ratio problems where the point is choosing the representation, and it works: tables for friendly multipliers, proportions for awkward ones, unit rates where a per-one value is needed, direct comparison only after both sides match. All eighteen checks recomputed here and correct, including the synthesis that compares concentration before scaling. The 32/32 is defensible on content. Two things the perfect score should not have survived: the Quick Answers bank prints '--' for the verified relations in problems 5, 9, 11 and 12 -- and because this sheet has no manual items, problems 5, 9 and 11 end up with no bank answer at all, including problem 11 whose entire task is to state the comparison. And the written prompts in 2, 3 and 7(a) are unflagged by an explicit decision recorded in final_response.md, which is the case the prompt's 'clearly label any genuinely open response' instruction was written for.
